note: Defects that are measured, not suspected. A row with no evidence field is an observation awaiting measurement and is marked severity 'unranked'.

defects.title: One-frame stall of 152 ms during the interactive walkthrough
defects.detail: The QA walkthrough sampled 45 FPS readings across 22 steps: 92 fps average, 6.55 fps minimum. A 6.55 fps sample is a ~152 ms frame. Not yet attributed — candidates are tile decode on the streaming thread, BVH construction on tile register, and the dev-tool spawn path. NOTE 2026-08-08: the walkthrough harness is not a benchmark. Headed Chrome plus a live ffmpeg encode plus ~26 resident MCP node processes produced avg 54 / min 0.08 fps on a build a headless fixed-camera probe measured at 100 avg / 86 1% low. Attribute this defect from the headless probe, not from walkthrough fps.

defects.title: Simulation order is emergent, and two vehicle registries cannot merge
defects.detail: CORRECTED 2026-08-08. The first version of this entry claimed the city read a stale pause state because ManhattanCity ran before GameLoop. That is false: GameLoop carries R3F renderPriority -100 (on the callback closing line, which is why a grep of the opening line missed it), so it writes rt.paused and the runtime clock before any priority-0 subscriber reads them. Ordering is correct today. What is real: (a) the order is bare integers in separate files with nine of eleven callbacks at the default priority, so their relative order is JSX mount order — undeclared, untested, and changed by moving a line; (b) the frame delta is clamped in six independent places all spelling 1/20 by hand (GameLoop MAX_DT, ManhattanCity, PlayerBody, CityLightingRig, DayCycleRig, SkyRig); (c) sim.registry.vehicles (Map, Phase 3A) and Traffic.vehicles (array, LION) are separate, so a city car cannot become the player car without a second overlapping instance. (c) is the only one with player-visible consequences.
defects.evidence: src/gameplay/simulation.ts; 19 tests; A/B in commit ee58bf966 (100.1 -> 100.0 avg fps, 86.5 -> 86.1 1% low, 3 passes headless)
defects.state: partially fixed — authority adopted by the city stage, one clamp now shared. The two registries (b) and the nine unmigrated useFrame callbacks remain.

defects.title: A night HDR lights the city at every hour; two material systems are dead
defects.detail: AUDITED 2026-08-08, docs/opus/LIGHTING_AUDIT.md. Nothing is fighting over background/fog — sky.js installs and weather.js drives, one subsystem. What is actually wrong: (a) NightEnvironment.tsx:23-58 sets scene.environment to a night HDR with dependency array [gl, scene], neither of which changes after mount, so a night map lights the city permanently regardless of the clock — the exact defect the brief names; (b) getBuildingNightMaterial has one call site, reachable only when ManhattanCity mode==="full", and the game mounts mode="tiles", so it has never rendered a streamed building; (c) SkyRig.tsx is imported by nothing. Streamed BLD_* actually get FacadeMaterial via streamer.injected.
defects.state: 0C.1 FIXED (18b38e540) — environmentIntensity follows nightFactor; measured 0 at midday, 0.1 at dusk, 0.2 at night. ManhattanCity now shares the canonical curve instead of a private copy with 90-minute-different shoulders. 0C.2 runtime assertion and 0C.3 adopt-or-delete for getBuildingNightMaterial/SkyRig remain.

defects.title: Street-level Manhattan is a stylised blockout, not a city
defects.detail: Flat extruded buildings with painted-on window rectangles, no facade depth or reveals, no entrances or storefronts, cone trees, untextured road with no kerbs, crossings, signals or clutter. This is the Stage 1-4 programme, recorded here so the gap is never implied away.

defects.title: Something outside this session checks out main mid-work
defects.detail: Observed twice on 2026-08-08, the second time DURING a turn: the working tree was switched from opus/hero-corridor-v1 to main while files were being edited. Symptom was 33 tests vanishing (simulation.test.ts 19, stat.test.mjs 14) because those files exist only on the branch. Reflog line: 'checkout: moving from opus/hero-corridor-v1 to main'. No work was lost — commits live on the branch and new untracked files survive a checkout — but a `git add -A` landing while main is checked out would commit to the wrong branch. Candidates: the second worktree at E:/temp projects/shenron-city-polish on branch polish/realism (locked), or one of the resident @gitkraken/gk MCP processes. Not attributed; not reproduced on demand.
defects.evidence: git reflog; test count 377 -> 344 with two files absent from the vitest file list
defects.state: open — mitigated by re-checking out the branch at the start of every turn

defects.title: A concurrent session left src/city/traffic.js with a parse error
defects.detail: Found at the start of the 21:10 turn. The working tree carried uncommitted edits I did not make across 7 tracked files (traffic.js, traffic.d.ts, vehicle-control.ts, vehicle-entities.ts, vehicle-lanes.ts, vehicle-replay.test.ts, vehicle-traffic.ts) plus 3 untracked new files (street-nav.js/.d.ts, graph-lane-provider.ts). It is the same consolidation this branch is doing, by a different route: a shared street-nav lane graph and 'ghosts' in Traffic for player-owned vehicles. src/city/traffic.js:109 does not parse, so the city pipeline cannot load and the game cannot boot. vehicle-replay.test.ts — their own Phase 3A determinism gate — also fails. Left completely untouched; snapshotted read-only to the session scratchpad (tracked.patch + the 3 new files). No git add -A while it is present. UPDATE 21:45 — traffic.js now parses and the game boots; they also adapted my vehicle-handoff differential test to import pointAt from their street-nav.js, and extended into ManhattanCity.tsx (installLaneProvider + trafficGhosts). Their design is a shared lane graph plus ghosts, which is complementary to the promotion module rather than a duplicate of it. 3 tests in their own new vehicle-session.test.ts still fail on ghost positions (~70 m out).
defects.evidence: vitest: 2 failed / 375 passed; PARSE_ERROR at src/city/traffic.js:109:12
defects.state: partially resolved — tree compiles and boots; ownership of the vehicle subsystem still undecided

defects.title: Times Square has no ground; the ocean shows through as a black void
defects.detail: CORRECTED 2026-08-09. The first version of this entry said "the ground plane renders pure black at midday" and blamed cityLightingUniforms.uCityHour defaulting to 21. Both wrong. Raycasting the black region names the mesh: WATER_ocean at y=0, 31-57 m from a camera at y=13.7. It is not a lighting bug and not a road bug — there is simply no island geometry at Times Square, so the sea plane beneath it is what you see. At the actual spawn point (1000, -3000) the same probe hits LAND_manhattan at y=11.99, colour #3f3e3c, exactly as it should. manhattan-collision.ts already documents the cause: "The Phase 2 source data has a genuine hole in the midtown-west band (no buildings, props or subway kiosks west of 6th Avenue — the Times Square plaza included)". The defect is that the hole is not hidden: the ocean should not be visible through missing land. Options are to extend the land mesh, to fill the hole in the Phase 2 source, or to stop rendering ocean inside the island footprint.
defects.evidence: raycast naming WATER_ocean at Times Square vs LAND_manhattan at the spawn point
defects.state: open — cause identified, fix not chosen

defects.title: The player's retargeted pose is contorted and his feet sit below the origin
defects.detail: After 05e841bf3 he stands — head 1.405 m above the feet, was -0.29 — but the pose is wrong: one arm raised straight up, one leg out to the side, and the foot bone sits about 0.77 m below the player origin so he is partly sunk into the pavement. The two fixes in that commit corrected the holder channel and the global Z frame; neither can correct per-bone rotations. scripts/retarget/bake-retarget.py retargets Quaternius clips onto the Sketchfab rig with world-space copy-rotation constraints, and the two rigs do not share a rest orientation. The fix is a proper re-bake against matched rest poses, in Blender. Patching further quaternions would be guessing at 89 bones.
defects.evidence: bone world positions in the running game; screenshot in the 05e841bf3 verification
